what: TSK-1419: the authors of the prophetic books marked as such on the Prophet list, beside what the text calls them. Added witnesses are in ../person-occupations.json; this file says why. Requests and the loader never read it.
decidedBy: an agent (claude-opus-5-5), 2026-11-16, on the project owner's word of 2026-11-16
ownerWord: TSK-1419, owner 2026-11-16: count the authors of the prophetic books (the Latter Prophets, and Daniel where our canon lists him) as prophets, with a separate mark 'author of a prophetic book', apart from 'called a prophet in the text'.
rules: Witness kind own-book is now the mark of the author of a prophetic book, held whether or not a text also calls him a prophet; a claim rests on a profession quotation, an own-book quotation, or both.

The books: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel and the Twelve (the Latter Prophets), and Daniel, whom the Protestant, Catholic and Orthodox canons place among the prophets (after Ezekiel); the Tanakh keeps him among the Writings, and his claim stands on Matthew 24:15 as before.

The own-book quotation is the verse of his book that names him as the one the word came to, who saw it or who wrote it: the superscription (1:1; Ezekiel 1:3), and for Daniel 7:1, 'then he wrote the dream'.

Every quoted name was read in BHSA and checked to be annotated to the record that holds the claim (ISA 1:1 isaiah, JER 1:1 jeremiah-6, EZK 1:3 ezekiel, DAN 7:1 daniel-2, JOL 1:1 joel-11, AMO 1:1 amos, JON 1:1 jonah, MIC 1:1 micah-4, HAB 1:1 habakkuk, HAG 1:1 haggai, ZEC 1:1 zechariah-13; HOS 1:1 hosea, OBA 1:1 obadiah-12, NAM 1:1 nahum, ZEP 1:1 zephaniah-3, MAL 1:1 malachi already held it).
An own-book quotation marks no word: the word that names the occupation comes only from a quotation that says it.
Not counted: Lamentations (no author named in it) and Baruch (Catholic and Orthodox canons; Baruch 1:1 names him as the writer, but neither the owner's word nor the Latter Prophets reach him).

added.alsoCalledInTheText: AMO 7:15 (the LORD's 'Go, prophesy'; his own 'I was no prophet' at 7:14 is said in his record's notes)

aaron.why: The owner's word of 2026-11-16 accepted the lead's proposal: 'Aaron is called one in Exodus 7:1 ... find why he was missed and fix that.' He was missed because the owner ruled on 2026-11-01 (PRB-1420 part 1, question 1) that Aaron is not a prophet there, since Moses tells Aaron what to say. Under the mark 'called a prophet in the text' the verse calls him so (נְבִיאֶךָ, 'your prophet'). Admitted on the newer word; the conflict with the older ruling is asked on TSK-1419. To keep the older ruling, drop this claim.
